name: Malware Scanner by Antivirus.ai – Shieldlume Security
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
Shieldlume Security by Antivirus.ai is a free WordPress malware scanner and security plugin from Plugins.shop. Review eligible core, plugin, theme and upload files, selected database content and finding evidence.

Try the Free & Pro interface demo | Owner guide | Compare Free and Pro

WordPress antivirus and malware scanning

  • Stream file hashes and high-risk patterns, including oversized files and PHP hidden in images.
  • Inspect selected WordPress database content.
  • Compare file integrity with eligible WordPress.org references.
  • On-demand/daily scans with saved progress and coverage details.

Login security and request protection

  • Two-factor authentication (2FA): authenticator codes, recovery codes or password plus passkey.
  • Optional login attempt limits, administrator enrollment and browser approval.
  • A WordPress request firewall with Off/Observe/Block, scoped exceptions and host recovery.
  • Separate login-page/XML-RPC request controls and an optional XML-RPC pingback switch.

Security reports and email alerts

Review evidence/severity and export findings or a JSON scan report. Optional critical email alerts and scan-end digests use your WordPress mail provider. Free local tools need no account, paid key or AI.

Optional sources: vulnerability data, host-managed ClamAV or signed hash indicators. Methods and limits.

The separate Pro add-on

Pro adds schedules, investigations, reports and reviewed file restoration with the same scanner. Online activation unlocks local tools; expiry/outages retain access, Disconnect removes it. Services/AI need separate consent/access. Free never downloads Pro code.

Related plugins by Plugins.shop

Separate optional tools:

  • Logged.ai – activity log: investigate supported site changes.
  • ClickClue – session replay: review eligible visitor journeys with privacy controls.

More from Plugins.shop.

External services and privacy

Activation starts no scan/provider request. Connections need separate permission/configuration; no usage/conversion telemetry. Privacy/operator | Terms | Data/retention/withdrawal. Details are bundled in docs/privacy-and-services.md and privacy.txt.

  • Antivirus.ai welcome/newsletter: separate unchecked choices send displayed domain, WordPress/PHP versions and language, or editable email/edition, to https://antivirus.ai/newsletter-api/v1/plugin-welcome/ . Consented reports refresh at most weekly plus edition changes; no source/findings/customer records. Email needs confirmation. Stop sharing in Protection settings; unsubscribe email separately. Sharing privacy, email privacy.
  • WordPress.org references: permitted jobs send component/version, core locale, server IP/timing for official data compared locally. Privacy.
  • Wordfence Intelligence: permitted/configured feed requests use your API credential and server connection, without source uploads. Saving a token does not enable requests. Terms, privacy.
  • Signed indicators: the configured publisher receives protocol/version metadata and server IP for permitted updates, not inventory/source/samples. Destination/policy appears before enabling; no publisher/corpus is included.
  • Local ClamAV: eligible bytes go only to a protected host daemon; the host maintains its engine/definitions, FreshClam requests and logs. Guidance.
  • Emerging Threats: permitted https://rules.emergingthreats.net/blockrules/compromised-ips.txt downloads normally run every 12 hours. The provider sees server IP/timing, not visitor IPs/content; matching is local. Licence, privacy.
  • Pwned Passwords: supported permitted checks send five SHA-1 prefix characters and server IP/timing to https://api.pwnedpasswords.com , never the password/full hash/username/email. Matching is local. Service, privacy.
  • Exposure checks: permitted HTTPS probes contact this site’s public WordPress address. Its host/CDN sees selected paths and server IP/timing; up to 512 bytes are compared transiently, not uploaded to antivirus.ai.
  • Email notifications: selected alerts/tests send content and recipient through your WordPress mail provider. Handoff is not delivery; interrupted/uncertain sends need review.

Free does not contact Pro/AI services. Separately licensed/consented Pro AI explains minimized detector metadata, not source files, and cannot approve repairs or verify infection. Service privacy, terms, AI privacy.

Chosen connections share only documented data. Hiding previews does not stop sharing; withdrawal can remain pending when unreachable. Handle exports/provider records/backups separately. Self-service software, without managed cleanup or response-time guarantees. Support.

Source code and third-party notices

Readable source/assets are bundled. Authentication/QR builds and MIT licences: vendor/auth/NOTICE.md. Space Grotesk OFL: assets/fonts/OFL.txt.
sections.installation:
1. Keep a backup. Install Free on single-site WordPress 6.8+ with PHP 8.3+.
  2. Review Setup guide. Scanning needs canonical local POSIX paths without symlinked components; Windows drive/UNC paths and Multisite are unsupported.
  3. Start a scan. Dashboard, WP-Cron or Continue scanning resume work; cron depends on traffic.
  4. Review findings/coverage, correct and rescan. Install Free before Pro; replace packages without uninstalling.
sections.faq:
Does Free automatically remove malware?

No. Free supplies evidence/guidance. Use trusted tools/backups for corrections; Pro supports reviewed eligible restoration.

Does it scan WordPress plugins, themes and the database?

Yes, within recorded limits. A changed checksum alone does not prove malware.

Why can a finished scan have limited coverage?

Structural limits are 2/8/16 MiB by PHP memory/time; unlimited PHP selects 16 MiB with resource guards. Settings offers an override. Hashes/high-risk patterns run in resumable chunks. Not fully scanned lists unfinished checks. ClamAV/repairs retain 2 MiB limits. No clean-site guarantee or maintained malware corpus.

Are two-factor authentication and a firewall included in Free?

Yes. Passkeys follow the password as a second factor. Filtering covers supported WordPress requests, not server/CDN or DDoS protection. Account protection needs HTTPS and compatible host/browser support.

Can I use another security plugin?

Test coexistence. General login limits suspend for known conflicts; passkey password checks remain protected. Busy/unavailable/full counters reject protected checks in 1.1.8. Protection guidance.

Do scans or alerts need an account or AI?

No. Alerts use WordPress mail; optional sources need configuration/permission. AI belongs to Pro.

What happens when I deactivate or uninstall?

Keep data is default; reinstalling can resume sharing. Stop sharing/unsubscribe separately. Settings > Data & uninstall offers guarded removal; see docs/data-uninstall.md.
sections.changelog:
1.1.10

  • Skip breached-password checks for unchanged profile passwords; retain checks for changes.
  • Use 16 MiB for unlimited PHP memory, guarded by observed system/cgroup headroom.
  • Bound larger structural checks by resources; report unfinished checks.
  • Fix literal-only webpack expression gaps; flag unusual JavaScript decoder/execution fragments.
  • Detect high-risk PHP in JavaScript comments/strings; distinguish benign examples.
  • Keep finding priority in saved/public summaries independently of coverage.
  • Clear active file-fragment checkpoints after exhausted retries, including busy-lease recovery.
  • Update Antivirus.ai policy links and scanner documentation.

Earlier releases: bundled changelog.txt.
